summary: This is a test suite for the robot pet family: it checks that a pet's battery can never be created outside the 0-100 range, and that each subclass (cat, bird, dog) builds correctly, performs its own talent, and still inherits charging from its parent class.

lines.code: from pet_talents import RobotPet, RobotCat, RobotBird, RobotDog
lines.text: The tests live in their own file and import the four classes from pet_talents.py, so the code under test stays separate from the code that checks it.
This stands in for the tests written earlier in the chapter, which are still part of TestRobotPet; only the two new battery tests are printed here.
Passing a deliberately illegal battery value is the point: the test proves the setter clamps -10 up to 0 rather than storing nonsense.
unittest runs setUp before every single test method, so each test gets a brand-new pet and cannot be affected by changes another test made.
This guards the override: if RobotCat ever forgot to define its own show_talent and fell back to the parent's generic version, this test would fail.
Charging a cat tests inheritance rather than the cat itself — charge is defined once on RobotPet, and each subclass test confirms it still works through the child.
